main_text.p: retundunt, instructas acies in fugam vertunt, tuam etiam Imperator impietatem compressurae sunt etiam si ad aliquod tempus extollaris.] Dolebant, & lachrymabantur, (inquit {b}Charysostomus[?]) in malis quae tunc fiebant, quasi universo mundo tutores dati essent, & ibidem in Martyrum Iuventini & Maximi persona loquens: Aripiamus, inquit, arma spiritualia, non opus jaculis & sagittis? &c. Sed quid interim de hoc Apostata Episcopi Ecclesiae luminaria? Lyberius hoc ipso tempore Episcopus Romanus, ad Athanasium{c} literas dedit, sed de Imperatore excommunicando, aut deponendo, ne verbum quidem, multo minus trucidando: Imo ipse Athanasius, ex Alexandria Imperatoris mandato profugere coactus, in eos qui illum circumsistentes moerebant & discessum ejus graviter ferebant, oculis coniectis: [{d}bonae estote animo filioli, inquit, nubecula est, breui euanescet.] Quasi dixisset; non ipsi eam dissoluite, sed ejus dissolutionem maturè euenturam[?] expectate. Post Imperatoris interitum, duas quidem Invectivas in eum scripsitSerm. in Iuventinum & Maximum tom.3.Rufinus lib.1. cap. 30.Socrat. lib. 3. cap.12.

page.notes: Cut-off right-hand page at the edge: only fragments of lines are visible, so it is not transcribed. Running head at top right reads LIB.III, not included in running_head. Note b reads "Serm. in Iuventinum & Maximum tom.3."; the marker letters in the text are at "Charysostomus" (b), "Athanasium" (c) and the bracketed passage (d). Doubtful readings: "Charysostomus" (print: Charyfostomus), "euenturam" (print looks like cuenturam). "Lyberius" and "Athanasium" are kept as printed. Left margin notes are in italic type where printed. The footnote marker d sits inside the bracketed passage and the margin note carries the same letter.
